data.narrative:
Exodys Energy is a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Carl Perez and Jean-Christophe Piroux that has raised $10M+. The nuclear energy sector contains 11 total comparable companies: 3 publicly traded (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Stage-progression valuation is the applicable methodology here. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a proxy for pre-money value, a standard Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $25M. This reflects typical venture progression patterns for early-stage deep-tech companies in capital-intensive sectors.

Peer-median comparison was not viable: while five same-sector comparables exist, insufficient datapoints at matching stage or valuation tier precluded reliable bracketing. Drawing on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given nuclear's unique capital and regulatory requirements.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M–$29M, with a median of $25M. This single-method result carries meaningful uncertainty around stage-progression multiplier assumptions and the absence of direct peer anchoring. Key uncertainties include technology maturity relative to named peers, path to next financing round, and regulatory de-risking progress—none of which the available data directly captures.
